topic: Vercel Sandbox architecture and transferable primitives

supports: Sandbox is a compute primitive for untrusted or user-generated code
Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM with its own filesystem and network
System-privileged workloads such as Docker, VPN clients, and FUSE are supported
Persistence is the default; snapshots, tags, drives, and multi-agent users are documented features
A sandbox is a durable name plus config; a session is one running VM instance
Stop snapshots the filesystem and the next SDK call resumes from the newest snapshot
Sandboxes provision in the iad1 region
Each sandbox has a dedicated guest kernel, which is stronger isolation than containers
A unique per-sandbox proxy CA is mounted and added to the system trust bundle
Containers run inside a sandbox do not inherit the proxy CA or its environment variables
Sandboxes are not intended for permanent hosting or long-term data storage
The CLI is modeled on the Docker CLI: list, create, run, exec, connect, copy, stop, remove, fork, config, sessions, snapshot, snapshots, drives
sandbox run --name resumes an existing sandbox or creates it, ignoring create-only flags
--stop and --rm control what happens when a command exits and are mutually exclusive
sandbox fork seeds from the source snapshot and config; env is not copied and tags fully replace
Snapshot retention flags: --snapshot-expiration, --keep-last-snapshots, --keep-last-snapshots-for, --delete-evicted-snapshots
Network policy flags: --network-policy, --allowed-domain, --allowed-cidr, --denied-cidr
Drives mount as drive:path[:read-write|read-only]
Interactive sessions extend the timeout unless --no-extend-timeout is passed
Per-plan caps: 4/8/32 vCPUs, 8/16/64 GB memory, 45 minutes vs 24 hours, 10 vs 10,000 concurrent sandboxes, 15 open ports, 32 GB disk
Default timeout is 5 minutes and each vCPU includes 2 GB of memory
Metered dimensions are active CPU, provisioned memory, creations, egress, and snapshot storage
Time waiting on I/O is not counted as active CPU
Inbound downloads are free; egress and exposed-port traffic are billed
vCPU allocation uses a dynamic quota that ramps with sustained use and decays after 10 idle minutes
Snapshots expire 30 days after last use by default
SDK v2 replaced anonymous ephemeral sandboxes with named persistent ones
Sandbox.getOrCreate with onCreate and onResume hooks is the documented dev-server pattern
Sandbox.fork from a base sandbox is the documented isolation pattern
sandbox.update({ports}) replaces the full port list rather than merging
A HackerOne program runs 18 August to 1 September 2026 with up to $1M available
Maximum payout per report is $50,000, for cross-tenant access
In scope: escaping the Firecracker microVM to the host or another tenant, and bypassing the sandbox firewall
Container-only escapes inside the guest are out of scope because enforcement is at the host
A working proof-of-concept through the @vercel/sandbox SDK is required
sb exposes up/down/clean but no stop-with-restorable-state or automatic resume
sb snapshot accepts only name, --force, --db-only, --instance, --label; there is no retention or expiration option
There is no fork command
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is set on the host in sandbox/commands/config_setup.py; no CA bundle variables are injected into instance containers
